questions.prompt:
(a) The scientists take measurements of several physical quantities at each location.
Complete Table 1.1 by stating the SI base unit for each quantity and identifying with a tick (✓) whether each quantity is a scalar or a vector. Use the space for any working.

(b(i)) At one location, the density of the air is 1.1 kg m⁻³. A spherical weather balloon is filled with a gas and released from rest. The balloon has radius 0.90 m.
Calculate the upthrust acting on the balloon when it is released.

(b(ii)) Explain why an upthrust acts on the balloon.

(b(iii)) The balloon has weight 19 N.
Calculate the magnitude of the initial acceleration of the balloon.

(c) A quantity c relating to the motion of the balloon is calculated from three measured quantities k, F and v using the formula
c = 2kF / v².
The percentage uncertainties in the measured quantities are given in Table 1.2.

Table 1.2
measured quantity | percentage uncertainty
k | 5%
F | 3%
v | 4%

The calculated value of c is 1.8.
Determine the absolute uncertainty in c.

questions.prompt:
(a) The battery has electromotive force (e.m.f.) 5.0 V and internal resistance 4.7 Ω. The current in X is I₁ and the current in Y is I₂.

The resistance of X is 100 Ω. The resistance of Z varies with the intensity of light incident on it as shown in Fig. 5.2.
State Kirchhoff's first law.

(b(i)) The intensity of light incident on Z is 130 W m⁻². The current in the battery is 38 mA. Show that the terminal potential difference of the battery is 4.8 V.

(b(ii)) Calculate the current I₂ in Y.

(b(iii)) Calculate the power dissipated in Y.

(b(iv)) The intensity of the light incident on Z decreases. State and explain the effect on the terminal potential difference of the battery.

(c(i)) State the number of electrons in a neutral atom of radium-228.

(c(ii)) A nucleus of radium-228 undergoes a series of decays to form nucleus X. During the process, 5 α-particles and 4 β⁻ particles are emitted. Determine the number of protons and the number of neutrons in nucleus X.
